messages.subject: Jackknife for follow-up tasks
parts:
Hi lavaan community,

I was looking for a function to perform the leave-one out Jackknife to then play with some follow up procedures (for example BCa CI). Unfortunately I didn't find anything suitable and therefore I programmed a function myself quick and dirty:

jackknife <- function(object,
                      FUN = "coef",
                      args = list(),
                      verbose = TRUE,
                      group.adjust = FALSE) {
 
 
  # Largely adopted from bootstrapLavaan
  lavmodel                  <- object@Model
  lavoptions                <- object@Options
  lavpartable               <- object@ParTable
  lavdata                   <- object@Data
 
  lavoptions$verbose        <- FALSE
  lavoptions$check.start    <- FALSE
  lavoptions$check.post     <- FALSE
  lavoptions$optim.attempts <- 1L
 
  if(FUN == "coef") {
    lavoptions$baseline     <- FALSE
    lavoptions$h1           <- FALSE
    lavoptions$loglik       <- FALSE
    lavoptions$implied      <- FALSE
    lavoptions$store.vcov   <- FALSE
    lavoptions$se           <- "none"
  }
 
  t0 <- do.call(FUN, append(object, args))
  n  <- sum(lavTech(object, "nobs"))
  u  <- list(matrix(NA, nrow = n, ncol = length(t0)), rep(NA, times = n))
  r  <- 1
 
  for(g in 1 : lavdata@ngroups) {
    for(x in 1 : lavdata@nobs[[g]]) {
     
      if(verbose) cat("Jackknife ", round(x / n, 2) * 100, "%\r", sep = "")
     
      jackdata               <- lavdata
      jackdata@ov$nobs       <- lavdata@ov$nobs - 1
      jackdata@nobs[[g]]     <- lavdata@nobs[[g]] - 1
      jack...@case.idx[[g]] <- lav...@case.idx[[g]][-length(lav...@case.idx[[g]])]
      jackdata@ov$nobs       <- lavdata@ov$nobs - 1
      jackdata@norig[[g]]    <- lavdata@norig[[g]] - 1
      jackdata@X[[g]]        <- lavdata@X[[g]][-x,]
      jacksamplestats        <- try(
        lav_samplestats_from_data(
          lavdata = jackdata,
          lavoptions = lavoptions
        ), silent = TRUE
      )
     
      refit <- lavaan(
        slotOptions     = lavoptions,
        slotParTable    = lavpartable,
        slotModel       = lavmodel,
        slotData        = jackdata,
        slotSampleStats = jacksamplestats
      )
     
      u[[1]][r,] <- do.call(FUN, append(refit, args))
      u[[2]][r]  <- g
     
      r <- r + 1
     
    }
  }
 

  if(group.adjust) {
    for(g in 1 : lavdata@ngroups) {
      for(c in 1 : ncol(u[[1]])) {
        rc <- unique(round(u[[1]][u[[2]] == g, c], 4))
        if(length(rc) == 1) u[[1]][u[[2]] == g, c] <- NA
      }
    }
  }

  u <- u[[1]]
 
  coef <- sapply(rep(1 : ncol(u)), function(x, u, t0) {
    t0 <- t0[x]
    u  <- na.omit(u[, x])
    n  <- length(u)
    c(
      bias = (mean(u) - t0) * (n - 1),
      se = sqrt(((n - 1) / n) * sum((u - mean(u))^2))
    )
  }, u, t0)
 
  try(colnames(u) <- names(t0), silent = TRUE)
 
  out <- list(
    t0   = t0,
    u    = u,
    bias = coef[1,],
    se   = coef[2,]
  )
 
  class(out) <- "jackknife"
  out
 
}

summary.jackknife <- function(object, dec = 3) {
  round(
    cbind(
      t0   = object$t0,
      bias = object$bias,
      se   = object$se
    ),
    dec
  )
}


# Example
HS.model <- '
visual  =~ x1 + x2 + x3
textual =~ x4 + x5 + x6
speed   =~ x7 + x8 + x9
'

fit <- cfa(HS.model, data = HolzingerSwineford1939, meanstructure = TRUE)
jk  <- jackknife(fit)
summary(jk)


This is just a prototype. Warning: The coefs may even be miscalculated.

I have 2 basic questions. If anyone wants to give me input, I would be very grateful:

(1) For the Jackknife, I need to update the lavaan data slot to do the resampling. I can find the utility function lav_data_update, but the documentation says "A list of (new) data matrices (per group) of the same size". This does not fit to the Jackknife. Is there another internal utility function for the problem? If not, is my solution (highlighted in yellow) sufficient or is this not a good idea?

(2) For multi-group models the procedure seems dubious to me (leave-one out). If a data set in one group is omitted, it obviously has no effect on the coefficients of the other group. "se" and "bias" seem to be biased by this. I did include a "solution" (highlighted in red). But this is naive and anything but good. Any ideas or references? I can't find anything related to this case.

Best

Christian

messages.subject: Re: Jackknife for follow-up tasks
parts:
Hi Christian,

How about this? In your call to lavaan() using slots, do not use `slotData` and `slotSampleStats`, and use the argument `data` directly. As far as I understand, if these slots are not supplied, then `data` (or other arguments like `sample.cov` and `sample.nobs`) will be used. lavInspect() can be used to retrieve the data used, with column names included.

Maybe you have already tried this and this did not work? if it didn't, I would like to know.

There may be a more efficient solution. Anyway, my two cents.

By the way, BCa is already available, though only for single group for now (https://lavaan.ugent.be/history/dot6.html). (Not yet mentioned in the help page, it seems.)

-- Shu Fai

thanks for your advice. To do this, you would need to supply the jackknife function with the data as an additional argument or generate a data.frame from the data slot. The former is very messy. I have also written a function for the latter. However, that seems to me to be the worse and more error-prone option.

Best 

Christian
